title: AI-Driven Anomaly Detection in Component Burn-In & Screening
department: Department of Space / Indian Space Research Organisation
description:
Background In high-reliability sectors (like space) electronic components undergo rigorous environmental stress screening (ESS), including Burn-In testing (operating components at elevated temperatures, e.g., 125°C for extended periods).
Traditional screening relies on static parametric pass/fail limits. However, 'latent defects'-components that pass the absolute limits but exhibit subtle, anomalous drift over time-often escape into final payloads, leading to catastrophic field failures.
Description Development of a predictive machine learning model that analyzes time-series parametric data (e.g., standby current Iddq, leakage currents, or propagation delays measured at intervals like 0h, 24h, 96h, and 168h to detect anomalous components.
Expected Solution Module A: The outlier detection system Static limits catch obvious failures. Participants need to develop a 'Dynamic' outlier detection system. If a lot has an average leakage current of 10µA, a part showing 45 µA is a massive anomaly, even if the absolute datasheet maximum limit is 50 µA.
Module B: Time-Series Drift Predictor Build a predictive regression model that takes Value_0h and Value_24h as inputs and forecasts Value_168h. If the predicted 168h drift rate exceeds a calculated safety slope, the system flags the component for early rejection.
Evaluation Metrics:
• Anomaly Detection Score: a False Negative (missing a defective part) is catastrophic, penalizing teams that let bad parts escape.
• Drift Prediction Accuracy : The mean absolute error between the predicted Value_168h and the actual hidden ground-truth values.
• Explainability : Can the model justify its classification to a QA inspector, or is it a complete black box?
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, machine learning, predictive applied to a smart automation problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Automation. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on model. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 19/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: AI-Driven Anomaly Detection in Component Burn-In & Screening

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that catches 'latent defect' electronic components, ones that technically pass standard pass/fail limits but show subtle, abnormal drift over time, the kind that currently slip through and cause catastrophic failures after deployment in space missions.
overview.why_it_matters: Static pass/fail thresholds miss components that are subtly different from their peers even while staying within spec. Catching that subtle drift before deployment directly prevents the kind of failure that's catastrophic once a payload is in orbit.
pain_points: Static parametric pass/fail limits miss components with subtle, anomalous drift that still technically pass.
Latent defects escaping into final payloads cause catastrophic field failures.
No dynamic, lot-relative outlier detection currently supplements static absolute limits.
overview.background: High-reliability electronic components undergo burn-in testing with static pass/fail limits, but subtle drift anomalies relative to a component's own lot can escape detection and cause catastrophic failures later, motivating dynamic, relative outlier detection.
overview.whats_being_asked: A predictive ML model with two modules: dynamic (lot-relative, not just absolute-limit) outlier detection, and a time-series drift predictor forecasting later-time-point values from early-time-point readings.
expected_solution: Module A: dynamic outlier detection relative to lot statistics, not just static absolute limits.
Module B: time-series drift prediction (e.g. forecasting 168h value from 0h and 24h values).
Validated detection of genuinely latent (subtle) defects that pass static limits.
Applicable to real parametric measurements (leakage current, propagation delay, etc.).

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough. Dynamic, lot-relative outlier detection combined with time-series drift prediction for latent-defect screening is a genuine, technically sophisticated improvement over standard static-threshold screening.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate-high. Achievable using established statistical outlier detection and time-series regression techniques, applied thoughtfully to this specific reliability-engineering problem.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine understanding of semiconductor reliability testing and statistical/ML modeling together, a specialized field.

innovation.note: Dynamic, lot-relative outlier detection plus drift forecasting is a genuine, well-motivated improvement over static-limit screening.

invention.note: Achievable using established statistical/ML techniques (lot-relative z-scores, time-series regression), real effort in correct application to this domain.

technical_feasibility.note: Both modules are achievable with a well-constructed synthetic dataset reflecting realistic burn-in test patterns.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly addresses a genuine, high-stakes reliability risk for space-grade components, catastrophic failure prevention.

architecture.note: Two distinct but related modules (outlier detection, drift prediction), well-understood statistical/ML patterns.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, genuinely achievable with a well-constructed synthetic dataset. Build your synthetic burn-in data with realistic lot-level statistics and embedded subtle drift anomalies to genuinely test both modules' effectiveness.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very well-specified two-module structure (dynamic outlier detection, drift prediction) with a concrete, illustrative example given in the problem statement (10µA average, 45µA outlier despite 50µA absolute limit).
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building outlier detection using only static absolute limits (missing the explicit 'dynamic, lot-relative' requirement) would fail the PS's core, explicitly-stated distinguishing ask.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Ensure your outlier detection is genuinely lot-relative (comparing a component against its own lot's statistical distribution, not just an absolute datasheet limit), this is explicitly, repeatedly emphasized as the key differentiator in the problem statement.

idea_0_4: Research real burn-in/ESS testing parameters (leakage current, propagation delay typical ranges and time intervals: 0h, 24h, 96h, 168h) to ground your synthetic dataset.
Construct a synthetic multi-lot dataset with realistic within-lot statistics and embedded subtle (lot-relative) outlier components.
Split: one person on Module A (dynamic outlier detection), one on Module B (drift prediction).
prototype_4_22: Build Module A: lot-relative statistical outlier detection (e.g. comparing each component against its lot's mean/distribution, not just absolute limits).
Build Module B: time-series regression predicting later-time-point values (168h) from early readings (0h, 24h).
Test both modules against your synthetic dataset's known embedded anomalies.
integration_22_30: Refine detection sensitivity based on discrimination test results, catching genuinely subtle lot-relative outliers without excessive false positives.
Connect both modules into one coherent screening report.
Test against your example-style case (a component within absolute limits but anomalous relative to its lot).
polish_30_36: Build a clear dashboard showing both modules' outputs, flagged components with lot-relative context and drift predictions.
Rehearse presenting your detection performance against your known synthetic ground truth for both modules.
Prepare to discuss the real reliability-engineering value of catching latent defects before deployment.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Demonstrate your system correctly flagging a component that passes the absolute datasheet limit but is a genuine statistical outlier relative to its own lot, exactly the example scenario given in the problem statement, live, that direct demonstration of solving the PS's own stated example is concrete, credible proof.

strengths: Very well-specified two-module structure with a concrete illustrative example to validate against.
Genuine, high-stakes reliability-engineering value for space-grade component screening.
weaknesses: Real burn-in test data isn't accessible, synthetic data quality and realism determine credibility.
Genuine lot-relative (not absolute-limit) detection requires deliberate statistical design, easy to accidentally build a static-threshold detector instead.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Balanced, with real attention to lot-relative statistical design specifically.
team_fit.approach: Research real burn-in test parameter ranges and construct your synthetic dataset with genuine lot-level statistical structure before building detection logic.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard statistical outlier detection and time-series regression model scaffolding.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Ensuring detection is genuinely lot-relative (not accidentally reverting to absolute-threshold logic), and understanding real semiconductor reliability testing context, that requires domain-aware statistical design.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded detector that defaults to absolute-limit thresholds rather than genuine lot-relative comparison would fail the PS's explicitly, repeatedly stated core requirement.

data_resource_availability.status: No real burn-in test dataset is accessible; a well-researched synthetic dataset grounded in real testing parameter ranges is the appropriate approach.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Construct synthetic data with realistic lot statistics and embedded subtle outliers, clearly labeled as synthetic but domain-grounded.

judge_qna.question: How is your outlier detection genuinely 'lot-relative' rather than just using absolute limits?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your specific statistical approach, comparing each component against its own lot's distribution (mean, standard deviation) rather than a fixed datasheet threshold, and demonstrate with the PS's own example scenario (10µA average, 45µA anomaly despite 50µA absolute limit).
judge_qna.follow_up: How does your detection threshold adapt across lots with genuinely different baseline characteristics?

judge_qna.question: How accurate is your drift predictor at forecasting 168h values from early readings?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Present your specific prediction accuracy against your synthetic ground truth, and discuss what makes a component's early drift pattern predictive of later failure.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your model's behavior for a component with an unusual but non-anomalous early drift pattern?
